Still Atlético came. Courtois made an extraordinary save from Romero and Konaté cleared off the line from Julián Alvarez. Real could do nothing, seemingly concerned only with limiting the damage. Oblak barely saw them. Real did not touch the ball in his area until they scored. Kylian Mbappé barely touched the ball anywhere. Inside Atlético’s half, a pigeon pecked the grass, uninterrupted.

When Diomandé did at last dash into that space with 15 minutes to go, Oblak saved, the opportunity to make a match of this wasted. Or so it seemed until, from a dead ball that was too late even for them, Rüdiger headed in to spark a rebellion that would prove brief and incomplete, unlike Simeone’s week.

Sports.title: ‘Mixed emotions’ for Farke as Leeds stay unbeaten with Crystal Palace stalemate
Sports.content:
Perhaps it is testament to the progress Leeds have made since returning to the Premier League just over a year ago that there was frustration at failing to move up to third after drawing with Crystal Palace. Instead, Daniel Farke’s team enter the prolonged international break in fifth and unbeaten, which is a fine achievement in itself.

Apart from Tyrick Mitchell’s disallowed goal, neither side gave much impression they would secure the points. For Palace, it was a first clean sheet of the season, having conceded at least twice in their opening four games, relieving pressure on Pierre Sage, while the hosts endured their first blank.

A victory by two clear goals would have meant a best-ever start to a Premier League campaign for Leeds but they were blunt in the final third. There was even a level of discontent amid a ponderous performance with fans chanting “forward” as they failed to replicate the thrashing of Newcastle on Monday.

“Mixed emotions,” Farke said. “We would have preferred to win, but the reality is it is 38 game days. It is not always magic nights under the floodlights, champagne football, you overrun the opponent and score goals for fun. Sometimes it is a scruffy Sunday afternoon when you have to dig in. This was one of these games.”

Farke is into the final year of his contract and signing a new deal is a priority for him and the club. His stature has grown over the past 10 months, with Leeds the fifth-best performing team in the division since December 2025 and the German will likely be rewarded in the coming weeks for bringing stability to the club as Leeds aim to build on strong foundations.

The most notable moment of the opening quarter here came when Walter Benítez took too long to distribute the ball. The referee, Adam Herczeg – making his Premier League debut and fully aware of the rules – awarded Leeds a corner as punishment. It was a tentative game in the autumn sunshine, lacking intensity and quality, with Ao Tanaka snatching at a shot the closest anyone got to threatening a goal.

Around the half-hour something akin to a football match broke out as nervousness was replaced by urgency. Jørgen Strand Larsen and Quinten Timber engineered a chance for Palace which was blocked and allowed Leeds to break through Noah Okafor down the left, although his cross was turned behind.

Palace had the greater quality, with Adam Wharton and Timber comfortable in possession in the middle of the park, while Yéremy Pino whizzed around in the hope of finding an opener. It was controlled play, as the visitors took their time in the buildup, although there was often very little at the end of it as James Trafford was left unthreatened.

View image in fullscreen James Justin stretches to block an effort from Eddie Nketiah. Photograph: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock

Leeds on the other hand would burst into life for brief moments as the full-backs flew forward, changing the dynamic in an instant but Palace’s centre-backs and wing-backs were built to deal with these rapid transitions, leaving Dominic Calvert-Lewin starved of service. Benítez could relax and re-read the laws of the game, having failed to face a single shot on target in the opening 40 minutes.

Palace pushed the fast-forward button at the break and Mitchell put the ball in the back of the net from a fine move down the right. The glory turned to anguish when the video assistant referee intervened to show Anan Khalaili was offside in the buildup, causing an eruption inside Elland Road.

Leeds were sluggish but the warning from Mitchell caused a reaction and they were almost ahead when Calvert-Lewin’s only real chance was saved by Benítez. The England striker was given too much space to get on the end of a cross but his sidefooted volley was weak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a touch of menace in the game as Tanaka and Wharton were booked in quick succession, the first for a cynical foul and the latter after lunging in late without a hope of winning the ball, ensuring Herczeg was far busier than the two goalkeepers.

Leeds were completely ineffective in open play, Ethan Ampadu engaged in a long-throwathon. Every few minutes he would trot to a sidelineto pick up the ball and hurl it into the box but Palace were alive to the danger. “We had many set pieces today, but also today we didn’t have the best quality of the delivery,” Farke said.

Palace edged the match and Daichi Kamada could have won it late on but his header drifted inches wide. Sage will be relieved to see his defence so well organised and untroubled after conceding 11 in the first four games, leading to plenty of early scrutiny on his appointment. “Especially when I read the social media, there’s a big pressure.” Sage said.

“But you know, I don’t care about that. I do my job with honesty, I give my best with my skills and my limits. And in the end, I have no regrets with what I do.”

Sports.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
Sports.content:
If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart.

That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years.

It has become a day that is no longer relished but dreaded, a failure not just of the two fanbases themselves but the authorities who have allowed the ugliness to fester, who have talked a tough game on sectarianism but done little in practice to combat it at source.

But nothing could spoil the mood of Derek McInnes’s team, humming after a tough start to the season and now able to toast a second victory over their rivals in the space of a week. For Celtic, sitting on three straight defeats, the silence will be filled with plenty of noises and voices over the coming international break: awkward questions and painful decisions that last season’s dramatic double may have forestalled but which can no longer be avoided.

The drop in standards over the opening weeks of this season has been alarming, and at 74 years of age Martin O’Neill is wise enough and self-aware enough to know that he may be as much part of the problem as part of the solution. For him, the next few weeks will be a time of “self-reflection” on his role and his future, on whether he truly has the energy in him for one last fight.

“It’s a matter of whether I can help the team, and I’ll have a look at that this week,” he said. “Every time things don’t go so well, age plays a part, and you know what, they may be right. I’m 110 in two years’ time. That may be time to wrap it up. But I’ll see how it goes.

View image in fullscreen Tempers flare between Rangers manager Derek McInnes (right) and his opposite number, Martin O’Neill, at Celtic Park. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Let me generalise a little bit. I got an opportunity to come back last October which I never thought would happen in my life. Winning the league, the game against Hearts, was one of the great moments of my managerial time. But even then, I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy, the desire. There’s nothing great about getting old, I’ll tell you that.”

What is true of O’Neill may also be true of a few of his players. Is Callum McGregor, club legend but now 33 years of age and increasingly off the pace, still fit for purpose? Does Liam Scales need replacing? Does Kieran Tierney still have the legs? What exactly is James Forrest still doing about the place? And in the meantime, would you remotely trust the Celtic board – still essentially hollow of footballing expertise – to oversee the required transition?

Not on this evidence. The summer signings – Kasper Høgh, Mika Baur, Camilo Durán – largely disappeared from view.

Quick Guide Roundup: Vrancken bewildered by VAR as Hearts frustrated at Kilmarnock Show Wouter Vrancken was left bewildered by the “strange” video assistant referee decision to rule out an early Hearts goal in their 1-1 draw at bottom-placed Kilmarnock. The Jambos thought they had gone ahead in the 11th minute when Laurent Mendy’s effort – which appeared to be going wide – was diverted into the net by the Killie defender Cathal McCarthy. But the VAR, Matthew MacDermid, advised Duncan Nicolson to rule it out as the ball had accidentally struck Mendy’s hand. Killie went ahead a few minutes later through a Jamie McCart own goal before Stephen Kingsley equalised in the 86th minute (pictured). But Vrancken cited similarities with the recent incident involving Manchester United’s Harry Maguire against Ipswich and felt Mendy’s inadvertent handball should have been rendered irrelevant by McCarthy heading the ball into the net. “For me, when it’s such a clear situation, it’s strange that the VAR comes in between and rules wrong,” said the Belgian. “We had a meeting last week about the laws of the game and the refs did their explanation but when you don’t see them applied in the game, then I’m thinking this is strange." Martin Boyle ended Hibernian’s losing streak at home after they fought back to claim a point in a 1-1 draw against Aberdeen. The Dons went ahead in the 17th minute with a composed finish from former Hibs striker Kevin Nisbet. Managerless Hibs – with John Potter in interim charge after David Gray’s midweek sacking – looked bereft of confidence for long spells. However, the Leith side – who had lost six successive games at Easter Road – earned a share of the spoils when Boyle levelled from the penalty spot in the 62nd minute after Jack Milne dragged Jason Kerr to the ground. Steven Pressley praised Joe Westley for the bravery he showed by playing in Dundee's 2-1 home win over Motherwell. The former Burnley striker fractured his cheekbone against Hearts a fortnight ago but declared himself available after deciding against having surgery. Instead, he played wearing a protective mask and nett Dundee’s opening goal from the penalty spot before Bradley Fink doubled their advantage. Alex Lowry pulled one back for the visitors just before the break but the home side held on. Pressley said: “Joe showed great courage. But he gave a wonderful performance, without any trepidation. Joe was fearless in everything he did and to score a goal is really important for him because he lives off them." Jim Goodwin hailed his side’s performance as the perfect tonic as Dundee United defeated St Mirren 3-0 in a one-sided contest in Paisley, with first-half goals from Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru. It was Goodwin’s first appearance in the dugout since a recent health scare and the United manager said: “On a personal note, it was great to be back. Certainly the best medicine that I could have hoped for was that type of result and performance." A stunning set-piece strike from Enes Alic in the sixth minute of stoppage time secured a dramatic 1-1 draw for 10-man St Johnstone against Falkirk. Falkirk took advantage of Cheick Diabaté’s 54th-minute red card to seize the lead through Ethan Ross on the hour. But Alic found the top corner from 25 yards to move Simo Valakari’s side up to sixth place. Press Association Photograph: Mark Runnacles/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

There was fury here but precious little focus, plenty of passion but no real patterns of play, no order to the chaos, no real idea of how to keep the ball or fashion a chance. Rangers dominated the central areas, where Dan Neil and Nicolas Raskin are already forging a formidable partnership and James Penrice merrily stomped all over the place.

O’Neill gambled on a back five, on Luke McCowan in a sort of withdrawn winger role, discarded both at half-time, rolled through his substitutions, but the plan never really emerged from the fog. Celtic are basically like the tangled ball of printer cables and headphone wires in the bottom drawer, where you’re never quite sure whether you’re unpicking the knots or making them tighter.

Naderi’s goal, bundled in from close range after Kim Min-su’s long-range effort was parried helpfully into his path by Viljami Sinisalo, was simply the most consequential emblem of Rangers’ superiority here. Emmanuel Fernandez got a rough ride early on, Tierney clipped the bar from distance and Ivor Pandur made a fine save from Colby Donovan early in the second half. That was basically it, as far as explicit threat went. Donovan’s header was the only Celtic shot on target.

“For a young team, it’s brilliant that they can take the good from this,” said McInnes. “Coming to places like this, it won’t get much more difficult. It’s only three points, but in the context of the season it was important for lots of reasons.” He knows, of course, that Rangers are not the finished article. But right now there is a power vacuum at the top of Scottish football and his improving side may as well be the one to fill it.

Sports.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
Sports.content:
Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death.

Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.

An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United player was adjourned again in July and has been scheduled to resume on 7 December after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England under-19 international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for the Sheffield United women’s team.

Olivia says the walk on Saturday, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence during the inquest. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.

“But I felt in the inquest it was lost that she was a person, she wasn’t an object that we were discussing. She’s a person, she’s a family member of ours [and] a person that’s sometimes been lost within the chaos surrounding her death really, so that’s the notion behind the walk. To claim her back, bring her home and protect her.”

A minute’s applause will be held before kick-off on Sunday at the Women’s Super League 2 fixture between Newcastle and Sheffield United. Discussing that anniversary, Olivia says: “We miss her the same every day, as I will on Sunday. The anniversary is always something that creeps up on us. It’s very emotional and it’s a time where we just reflect, but we do so much throughout the year so she really is at the heart of pretty much every single day. Not a day goes by where we don’t think about her.

View image in fullscreen Sheffield United and Maddy Cusack’s family paid tribute at Bramall Lane shortly after her death. Photograph: Richard Callis/MB Media/Getty Images

“There can be days when you just feel absolutely drained and you know you don’t quite know what the right thing to do is, but I think the way that we just get through it is that we remember who she was as a person. She loved her life, she loved trying new things and just enjoying life’s simple pleasures, we try and embody that on every day, not just the anniversary.

“I really do encourage people to, as difficult as it can be sometimes, share the photos, share the memories, bring her up in conversation wherever you can, talk about her, and between all of us, you know her legacy will live on.”

The family have already endured eight full days of evidence, after the hearing began belatedly on 29 June, but the discovery of additional documents led the proceedings to be paused until December. The coroner apologised to the family for yet another delay. The case had been set previously to start being heard on 5 January 2026 after additional postponements in 2025.

“It’s been really difficult,” Olivia said of the delays. “It’s not something that any of us anticipated to happen. It’s very confusing and it can be very frustrating, the length of time it’s taken, it can be difficult to work that out and to know how you should be feeling and the process of it. However, we know that for the right outcome it has to be taken seriously. They need the time to come together and really get an outcome.

View image in fullscreen Maddy Cusack was also remembered during the Premier League match between Sheffield United and Newcastle. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

“It feels as though she can’t be at peace until it’s finished. And I do feel that’s quite upsetting to think about and to work through. It needs to come to a conclusion.”

Olivia said she would “channel Maddy’s energy” during the 29-mile walk on Saturday, when a group of about 15 family and friends travelled in the reverse direction to another fundraising walk in February 2024 from Pride Park to Bramall Lane.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This time they set off from Sheffield at 5.30am. A fundraising page for the walk had surpassed £1,100 as of Saturday afternoon. Olivia described that tally as “incredible – £1,000 is just amazing, it’s more than I ever expected” and said: “Particularly with it being Maddy’s anniversary, it’s going to be very much a mental challenge as well as a physical one, so it gives you that extra motivation to make the people who’ve donated proud.”

The money is being raised for the Maddy Cusack Foundation, which is helping a range of causes targeting women’s and girls’ football and “letting girls be seen within sport”.

“We provided Derby County Community Trust with a series of bursaries for girls and families who struggle with the financial prospects of becoming dedicated to their football. It’s a helping hand for any child that needs that extra sort of funding, taking away the barriers that they might face.”

The foundation has also partnered with the Stockport County left wing-back and former Derby, Sheffield United and Nottingham Forest player defender Ben Osborn’s organisation Elite Football Development, which aims to inspire young people through sport and education.

“They work with girls and boys but we sponsor the girls’ side of things, which is focused around post-16 study, and allows girls to gain qualifications alongside being able to train and live the life of a professional footballer. We were really keen to get involved in this as Maddy was really passionate about education.”

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline on 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counsellor. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

Sports.title: Hayen must worry about his Burnley future but fans’ fears are existential
Sports.content:
The greatest moments of Burnley’s history were beamed on to a big screen before kick-off at Turf Moor, accompanied by famous lines of commentary. The final one, the moment promotion was sealed under Scott Parker in April 2025, was soundtracked by: “Burnley are back in the big time.” That feels a long time ago now, with a return to the Premier League a remote prospect.

Burnley appeared to have this game against Derby sewn up, leading through Zeki Amdouni’s first-half header, but a stunning stoppage-time strike from the Rams’ substitute Mo Fuseini soured the Turf Moor mood. It means Burnley’s winless home league run could now reach a year, the Clarets last tasting victory at Turf Moor on 18 October 2025. Their last win in any competition in 90 minutes was on 11 February.

The draw left Nicky Hayen, the under-fire head coach, under scrutiny, though the majority of fans will direct their anger towards Alan Pace, the chair, given the financial problems and off-field turmoil that plagued the club during a disruptive summer.

Hayen vowed to fight for his future and revealed he would talk with Pace, though could give no assurances he will remain in charge for the next game at Watford on 10 October after the extra-long international break. “I can understand the fans are angry after a start like this, it’s not what they want to see from their team or from myself,” he said. “It’s my responsibility. But I’ve always shown resilience and I’m always going to fight. We need this [international] window to change a lot of things.”

View image in fullscreen Mohammed Fuseini celebrates scoring a late equaliser for Derby. Photograph: Alfie Carling/PPAUK/Shutterstock

In his programme notes before the game, Pace called for fans to “unite and show togetherness”, after they had chanted for his removal during the home defeat by Bristol City a fortnight ago. There was some early encouragement for Hayen’s team as they sought to make inroads against Derby. Although a lack of thrust in the final third was evident at times, Burnley made the breakthrough via Amdouni’s forehead, the forward peeling around the back post to nod home Lucas Pires’s corner.

Hayen, who was managing Haverfordwest County in the Welsh Premier four years ago and was not Burnley’s first choice to replace Parker, celebrated. Having been accused of muddled selections in his tenure so far, he had made some brave calls, dropping the club captain, Kyle Walker, and struggling goalkeeper Max Weiss, and recalling Marcus Edwards, who had been jettisoned after featuring in the campaign’s opening two games.

Those decisions were nearly vindicated, right up to the moment Fuseini pounced, leaving Hayen to bear the brunt of more fan criticism. “It is really difficult [to take],” he said. “You saw the reaction of the players after the game, sitting on the ground, disappointed. We wanted to give the fans the win, I wanted this for them, I can accept their frustration. I want to give back to the fans, I feel we can give back a lot. You saw we were close, we wanted to do it just before the international break.”

Quick Guide López fires Wolves to derby win over West Brom Show Fer López fired Wolves to a 1-0 win against arch rivals West Brom in a bruising Black Country derby on Sunday. Lopez punished a blunder by Albion defender Nat Phillips to score his fifth goal of the season in the second half of the Championship clash at Molineux. It was no more than Wolves deserved after Albion keeper Max O’Leary had kept West Brom in the game during the first half with three outstanding saves. Albion rarely threatened to snatch an equaliser in the first Molineux meeting between the west midlands rivals in five years. After fears of a repeat of the serious crowd trouble that marred their previous showdown at West Brom two years ago, the derby passed off peacefully inside the stadium. Elsewhere in the Championship, Bolton twice came from behind to win 4-3 in a thriller at Norwich. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The break may represent a chance for Hayen, if he remains, to regroup, though for Pace and the board there remain unanswered questions about the £142m of external debt the club owes, as well as the £81m owed by his firm ALK Capital to the club itself after a leveraged buyout in December 2020. Comparisons with the Glazers’ takeover and ownership of Manchester United have been made. James Holroyd’s recent departure, after 15 months as chief executive, feels reflective of the worsening malaise in the boardroom. Holroyd previously worked under the Glazers at United.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Despite two promotions under the current regime (and three relegations) the Clarets’ financial situation has deteriorated, with some fans now harbouring genuine fears of total extinction if debts are not repaid. Parachute payments may help for a time, but Burnley no longer have the cash reserves they boasted in their debt-free era before Pace and ALK when they enjoyed five successive seasons in the Premier League under Sean Dyche. Such stability now feels a world away and problems are spilling on to the pitch. Money has been spent on transfers, with squad turnover high in recent seasons, but there was particular concern when the £20m made from the sale of Zian Flemming was not reinvested in a new striker, with 39-year-old Jamie Vardy hastily arriving on a free transfer after the transfer window had closed.

View image in fullscreen Zeki Amdouni sprints off to celebrate his goal for Burnley. Photograph: Alfie Carling/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Hayen sent on Vardy and loan signing Largie Ramazani to retain a counterattacking threat against Derby late on, as Burnley hung on. But with a slender lead going into stoppage time, their confidence appeared brittle. Goalkeeper Grégoire Coudert had been forced into a couple of late interventions after Ryan Hedges should have equalised for Derby on the hour mark.

Then, just when it seemed Burnley’s winless streak would be broken, the rocket from Fuseini snatched two points away, leaving them bottom of the Championship. “It’s hard to take,” said Hayen. “It’s frustrating.”

Sports.title: Celtic supporters’ bus goes up in flames near stadium as fans evacuated in terrifying scenes
Sports.content:
Celtic supporters’ bus goes up in flames near stadium as fans evacuated in terrifying scenes

A bus carrying Celtic supporters caught on fire following Sunday's Old Firm derby against Rangers.

Martin O'Neill's side were beaten 1-0 at Celtic Park, with Ryan Naderi scoring the only goal of the game.



2 Celtic fans were evacuated for a bus after it caught on fire following Sunday's Old Firm derby Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

There were distressing scenes near to the stadium following the match, though.

Footage shared on social media showed a coach ablaze on the Clyde Gateway (A728) close to the Emirates Arena.

The venue is situated opposite Celtic Park, with the coach catching on fire as it left the stadium.



Supporters were evacuated from the vehicle as emergency services rushed to the scene to tackle the blaze.

Police Scotland have since confirmed there were no injuries suffered.

It is understood the fire had started at the rear of the bus before spreading.



Thick plumes of black smoke could be seen high in the air above the coach during the incident.

The fire took place at around 2:30pm on Sunday, less than an hour after the final whistle.



As two fire engines arrived to tackle the fire, fans gathered on the pavement opposite.

Supporters from the Motherwell 9 in a Row Celtic Supporters' Club had hired the bus from McLean's Coaches of Aidrie, The Sun reports.

Once the fire had been put out, the vehicle was loaded onto a recovery lorry.

As a result of the blaze, the back of the coach had been destroyed.

McLean's Coaches statement

McLean's Coaches have claimed the fire was started deliberately in an act of vandalism.



A statement shared to social media read: "We are aware of an incident involving one of our coaches on the Clyde Gateway earlier today.

"We understand there were passengers onboard at the time, including families and young children, and fully appreciate how frightening the incident must have been for everyone involved. Thankfully, everyone was able to get off the coach safely.

"Based on the initial information and images we have received, we have reason to believe the incident may have been caused by vandalism.

2 A statement has been released by the coach's owners claiming the fire was started deliberately Credit: Getty



"To be absolutely clear, this is not an allegation against the passengers or the supporters’ club.

"The matter has been reported to the relevant authorities, who are investigating the circumstances.

"The vehicle has been recovered and will undergo a full inspection. We would like to thank the emergency services and everyone who assisted at the scene."

Sunday's Scottish Premiership meeting at Celtic Park was the second Old Firm derby in seven days between the bitter rivals.



Rangers beat Celtic 3-0 at Ibrox last weekend in the quarter-finals of the Scottish League Cup.

Their latest clash saw the visitors end their opponents' 100 per cent league record this season as well as cutting their lead at the top of the table to two points.

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill drops huge hint over Celtic future with revelation after Rangers defeat
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill has admitted he is considering his future as Celtic manager after their third successive defeat.

The Scottish champions were beaten by Old Firm rivals Rangers for the second time in a week on Sunday.

3 O'Neill has admitted he is considering his future as Celtic manager Credit: Getty

Ryan Naderi's first half strike clinched a 1-0 victory at Celtic Park to end the Hoops' perfect start to the new Scottish Premiership season.

It followed a 3-0 win at Ibrox in the Scottish League Cup last weekend.

Meanwhile, O'Neill's side suffered a reverse at home against Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday night.

Celtic have now lost four matches in all competitions this season, as many as they did in 35 games under O'Neill last term.

O'Neill on his Celtic future

The 74-year-old was handed a one-year deal in June after guiding Celtic to a league and Scottish Cup double.

It followed his return for a second spell as caretaker manager in January of this year.

His time in permanent charge could soon be over, though, with O'Neill telling reporters: “I'm not immune from criticism. Far from it.

"Absolutely. They [fans] have every reason to ask, can you turn this round? Can you change the whole thing?

"It's not the first time I've been questioned about my managerial time. So, I'll have a look at it. I will reflect and see.

"Asking what I, myself, [can do], is the main thing. Asking what I can do to help the team. That would be the most important thing for me to see.

3 Rangers beat Celtic for the second time in a week on Sunday Credit: Getty

"I genuinely will reflect and see. It's a matter of whether I can help the team. If that's the case.

"The manager’s supposed to be able to do that and I will have a look at that there this week.

"That every single time that something crops up, things don't go so well, age plays a part. And you know what? They may well be right.

"I'm 110 in two years' time, so that might be a time to wrap it up. Listen, we've lost some big games. There's no question about it.

"I personally think every game here is big. We lost a European game. We lost the big match out in LASK and, here, two defeats against us. Of course you have to question it.

"I will reflect on the games. I'll obviously speak to the board. And, you never know, they may want to speak to me, but I'll see.

3 O'Neill was handed a one-year deal in June after a league and cup double last season Credit: Getty

"I've got some time to do that there. I will try and get a couple of days away and see how it goes."

O'Neill previously spent five years in charge of the club between 2000 and 2005.

During that time, he won seven trophies including three league titles and reached a UEFA Cup final.

When do Celtic play next?

Celtic do not return to action for three weeks due to the first international break of the season.

Their next match will see them travel to face Motherwell on October 11.

As well as their latest run of losses, O'Neill's side were also dumped out of the Champions League last month.

Celtic were beaten 5-4 on aggregate by LASK in the play-off round.

Despite winning the first leg 3-0 at Celtic Park, they were unable to advance to the league phase.

Instead, Celtic suffered a 5-1 defeat after extra time in Austria, causing them to drop into the Europa League.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick issues Marcus Rashford injury update as star forced off ahead of crucial England games
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick issues Marcus Rashford injury update as star forced off ahead of crucial England games

Marcus Rashford is at risk of missing England's upcoming Nations League fixtures after he was forced off against Fulham.

The Manchester United forward was taken off during the second half at Craven Cottage on Sunday.

3 Rashford is a doubt for England's upcoming matches after he was forced off on Sunday Credit: Getty

It comes less than a week before the Three Lions return to action for the first time since the World Cup.

Thomas Tuchel named his 27-man squad for the matches against Spain, Czechia and Croatia on Friday.

Rashford was amongst those included by the England boss after his bright start to the season.

However, he could now be forced to withdraw from the squad due to a potential injury blow.

The 28-year-old was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the 77th minute of United's 1-1 draw against Fulham.

His final contribution of the afternoon saw Rashford slip over prior to being withdrawn by Michael Carrick.

Rashford injury update

The Red Devils boss was unable to confirm the extent of the injury following the match.

When asked by talkSPORT's Alex Crook if there is a chance Rashford will have to pull out of the England squad, he said: "I really don’t know.

"As you can imagine, at the end of the game I’ve spoken to the players and not really got to that stage. So we’ll just have to wait and see."

England face Spain at Wembley Stadium on Saturday, September 26 as they begin their Nations League campaign, live on talkSPORT.

3 Carrick admitted he does not know the extent of Rashford's injury after the match Credit: Getty

Rashford featured six times for the Three Lions at the World Cup in the summer.

He ended the tournament with one goal and one assist as Tuchel's side finished third, their best performance since 1966.

Meanwhile, he has made six appearances in all competitions for United so far this season.

It follows his return to the fold after loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona.

Rashford has featured in all five Premier League matches this term, starting the last four.

However, he has yet to score or provide an assist during the current campaign.

3 Rashford was included in Tuchel's 27-man England squad on Friday Credit: Getty

Sunday's visit to Fulham saw him draw a blank once again, with the Red Devils rescuing a point late on.

Matheus Cunha's equaliser cancelled out an own goal from Lisandro Martinez to leave United 12th in the table.

Sports.title: Man United missed massive trick not re-signing Danny Welbeck as 5/10 forwards flounder
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha’s fortuitous late leveller eases some of the pressure on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick heading into the international break.

However, a limp 1-1 draw against a Fulham side who started the day bottom of the table and who are still searching for their first Premier League win under new manager Alvaro Arbeloa does not paper over United’s early-season cracks.



5 United were perhaps fortunate to come away with a point in what was a lifeless performance at times Credit: Alamy

The harsh reality for the travelling fans, who booed loudly when Carrick took off their favourite son Kobbie Mainoo, is this was another toothless attacking display where their team looked far too open out of possession, as has become a recurring theme.

Lisandro Martinez’s comical own goal to gift Fulham the lead 18 minutes into the second half sums up the meandering manner in which United have started their campaign.

The fact that when they were in need of a game-changer off the bench at 1-0, Carrick could only call upon the willing but limited Joshua Zirkzee exposes one of many big flaws in the Red Devils’ summer recruitment.



With Benjamin Sesko absent due to injury, Carrick opted once again to start Cunha as the false no.9.

The only other options available were Marcus Rashford or Bryan Mbeumo, but, like Cunha himself, are both much more affective out wide.



Having to reintegrate the previously unwanted Rashford, mainly due to his huge £350,000-a-week wages, means Cunha has had to sacrifice playing in his preferred inside-left role.

If anyone deserved the slice of luck that came via his hopeful shot being deflected past a stranded Bernd Leno in the 89th minute, it was the Brazilian.



Cunha was the best of United’s attacking contingent throughout the afternoon and had earlier been denied by the post.

But that does not disguise the fact Rashford’s end product since returning to his boyhood club has left a lot to be desired.

5 Rashford hasn't scored in any of his six games this season Credit: Getty

A lot has been spoken and written about the Old Trafford hierarchy’s transfer window failure to provide Carrick with the extra defensive cover he clearly needs, especially in the full-back areas.



But, serious questions also need to be asked as to why they didn’t make any meaningful attempt to add to their striking options.

Zirkzee has proved he is not good enough to get United back to where they publicly aspire to be and Sesko is not the finished article even when fully fit.

At the start of last season United toyed with the idea of re-signing their former academy graduate Danny Welbeck from Brighton but talks with his advisors quickly tailed off.

When it became clear Brighton were willing to sell Welbeck to Chelsea this summer, and sources have told me he went for as little as £4million, United should have been fighting hard to hijack the deal.



Not only could Welbeck do a job leading the line, but he would also bring much-needed character and leadership to a dressing room that, from the outside at least, still looks lacking in that department.

If Carrick had his former teammate at his disposal at Craven Cottage then United would surely have posed much more of a goal-threat and maybe would have come away with a bigger share of the points.

5 Man United opted not to bring back Welbeck 12 years after he left Old Trafford, and now they're paying the price Credit: Getty

Manchester United player ratings

5



Groves: Carrick 'won't last half a season'

In a conversation with me immediately after the final whistle, talkSPORT's Perry Groves said he believes Carrick's days as United boss are numbered.

"I'm looking at this and I said Man United are a half-and-half team," Groves said.

"When they close down, they do it half-heartedly. When they drop deep, they don't close the ball down when it's in their own final third.

"I can't see Michael Carrick lasting half the season."

"They had a bit of urgency when they were 1-0 down, but it's a different scenario," Groves continued.



"When you're one or 2-0 down, it's easier because the opposition sits deeper, so you then think you'll take chances.

5 Carrick's men have won just one of their five league games this term Credit: Getty

"They should be doing that before they go 1-0 down in the 63rd minute."

"From a player's point of view, I think they're nice to play against," Groves added.



"I don't think they really test you. We've seen it in the first half where Fulham played through them fairly easily. There was a period of 20 minutes in that first half where every time Fulham went forward, they looked like they were going to score.

"If Gonzalo Garcia had his boots on the right feet in the first half, this could have been a lot worse.

"I just think Manchester United have got away with it."

Sports.title: Why Sunderland did not get penalty after Elliot Anderson handball in incident you may have missed
Sports.content:
Why Sunderland did not get penalty after Elliot Anderson handball in incident you may have missed

Sunderland were controversially denied a penalty during their defeat to Manchester City on Sunday.

The Black Cats' 5-3 defeat at the Etihad Stadium could have been different had Elliot Anderson been penalised for a handball inside the City penalty area.



2 Sunderland were denied a penalty for handball during their loss to City Credit: Getty

The midfielder appeared to swat the ball away with his hand whilst jostling for possession with Enzo Le Fee.

Anderson then hooked the ball clear as the Sunderland man appealed for a spot-kick.

Sunderland denied a penalty

His calls for a penalty fell on deaf ears, though, with referee Robert Jones opting not to award a spot-kick.



VAR also decided against intervening to overturn the on-field decision.

talkSPORT understands the officials deemed Anderson's handball as accidental. As a result, he was not penalised despite the ball hitting his hand.



That's not how Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris saw it, saying post-match: "It was hard to see that as not a handball.

"It is what it is and we have to accept the decision. It's hard to comment."



Busy afternoon for VAR

It was not the only contentious decision VAR had to deal with during the match.

Erling Haaland's late strike was initially ruled out for offside by the assistant referee.

However, a VAR review determined Josko Gvardiol had been onside during the build-up, with the goal awarded.

Explaining the decision on X, the Premier League Match Centre said: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside and determined that Gvardiol was in an offside position in the build-up and recommended that the goal was awarded."



Haaland's effort nine minutes from time completed the scoring on a frantic afternoon in Manchester.

City had twice been pegged back by Brian Brobbey during the first half after Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki put them ahead.

A brace from Antoine Semenyo either side of half-time established a two-goal advantage, though.

Brobbey completed his hat-trick just two minutes later to reapply the pressure to Enzo Maresca's side.



Haaland's fifth Premier League goal of the season was ultimately enough to clinch all three points for his side and maintain their 100 per cent record.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told he’ll be sacked by January as Gary Neville slams ‘worst ever’ Manchester United
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's days as Manchester United manager are numbered, talkSPORT's Perry Groves said following a 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Matheus Cunha's deflected strike in the 89th minute ensured the Red Devils left Craven Cottage with a point after Lisandro Martinez's comical own goal put the hosts in front.

4 Cunha's first league goal this season spared United's blushes Credit: Getty

The result means United have won just once from their opening five league matches and, perhaps more worryingly, are still yet to keep a clean sheet.

Groves, who was at Craven Cottage on commentary for talkSPORT, was especially critical of United's urgency, or lack of, throughout the contest.

"I'm looking at this and I said Man United are a half-and-half team," Groves said.

"When they close down, they do it half-heartedly. When they drop deep, they don't close the ball down when it's in their own final third.

"I can't see Michael Carrick lasting half the season."

What did Perry Groves say about Manchester United's display against Fulham?

Groves added that the draw, which helped United to their fifth point of the season, was 'papering over the cracks'.

"They had a bit of urgency when they were 1-0 down, but it's a different scenario," Groves continued.

"When you're one or 2-0 down, it's easier because the opposition sits deeper, so you then think you'll take chances.

"They should be doing that before they go 1-0 down in the 63rd minute."

Fulham could, and perhaps should, have been ahead by more when Martinez inadvertently poked the ball into his own net after Senne Lammens parried Calvin Bassey's effort.

4 Carrick was handed a permanent deal before the end of last season Credit: Getty

Unfortunately for the Cottagers, summer signing Gonzalo Garcia seemed to have left his scoring boots elsewhere as he spurned a number of good chances.

But the fact Garcia enjoyed a number of promising opportunities against United had Groves believing rival players now circle matches against the Red Devils in their calendar, such is the number of high-quality chances they tend to give up.

Manchester United 'got away with it' against Fulham

"From a player's point of view, I think they're nice to play against," Groves said.

"I don't think they really test you. We've seen it in the first half where Fulham played through them fairly easily. There was a period of 20 minutes in that first half where every time Fulham went forward, they looked like they were going to score.

"If Gonzalo Garcia had his boots on the right feet in the first half, this could have been a lot worse.

"I just think Manchester United have got away with it."

4 The Red Devils haven't convinced in their opening five fixtures Credit: Getty

Neville: 'The worst 15 minutes from Man United ever'

Man United's performance in the first part of the second half had club legend Gary Neville seething as he was left astounded by the team's lack of work-ethic.

Neville said on commentary for Sky Sports: "I’ve watched Man United since the age of 5 and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen them pla."

Neville added after the game: "Both teams were the same. I called them mannequins. They were mannequins. I've never seen a United team walk around as much as that. No alertness, no aliveness. No 'on your toes'. You should always be on your toes.

"Always shifting up two or three yards. They were just walking when Fulham were in possession. Fulham had 46 passes in the first couple of minutes to get their first shot.

"46 chances - Fulham against Man Utd. I don't know how many over-ten-pass sequences Fulham had in that game, but the international break has come at a great time. There needs to be a rebalance."

Neville continued: "I've never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that. Michael has just said there was nothing wrong with the team's energy.

4 Man United's application at Craven Cottage was a red flag for Neville Credit: Getty

"Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them; he's loyal, he wants his players to work for him, and obviously there's a long way to go in the season."

For Carrick, the international break may have arrived at an opportune time given the stark contrast in results from when he first took over to now.

The brutal stats exposing Manchester United's downturn under Michael Carrick

In Carrick's 17 league games at the helm last term, United averaged 2.3 points per game.

But that figure has dropped to just one point per game this season, hinting that something is not going according to plan within his set-up.

In another alarming stat, the five points accrued by United under Carrick this term is their joint-fewest from the first five games of a Premier League season.

According to talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook, United's bleak start is perhaps emblematic of their malaise in recent years.

"There's just an acceptance of these low standards at Manchester United, that dropping two points away from home at Fulham isn't a disaster that it maybe once was," Crook said on commentary.

"I think what Michael Carrick has got to do, and he did it in the second half of last season, is change the whole mindset in that dressing room."

Carrick now has multiple weeks to re-wire the mentality of his players before they return to action on October 10 at home against Tottenham Hotspur, who sit bottom of the table.

Sports.title: EFL club buy one million bricks salvaged from hospital for new stadium
Sports.content:
EFL club buy one million bricks salvaged from hospital for new stadium

Birmingham City have taken another step towards the completion of their new 62,000-capacity stadium.

The Championship club have purchased one million bricks from the former City Hospital to help with construction of the ground.

3 Birmingham have purchased one million bricks from City Hospital for their new stadium Credit: PA

It comes as they plan to leave St. Andrew's by 2030 as part of a £2billion regeneration project.

The redevelopment in the Bordesley Green area of Birmingham will see the introduction of a new Sports Quarter.

Backed by their owners Knighthead, Blues will leave their home of 120 years, which currently holds 29,400 fans.

Birmingham stadium latest

Ahead of the move, bricks have been bought from the city's historic former hospital.

City Hospital closed in 2024 after more than 130 years in operation, having been founded in 1887.

The bricks have been cleaned by specialists ahead of being used for the new development.

It is understood the hospital bricks will form part of the 12 brick chimney-style towers at the new stadium.

Images of the planned venue show the towers on display in a nod to the brickwork which used to sit on the site.

A record of how the bricks were manufactured, stored and transported will also be displayed once the stadium is completed.

The club previously revealed their aim to have moved into their new home by the start of the 2029/30 season.

3 The hospital bricks will form part of the 12 chimney-style towers in the stadium design Credit: Collect

However, their flexible completion goal is currently during 2030 for the ground, which was unveiled in November last year.

Previous stadium plans

Birmingham previously unveiled plans for a new stadium during their time in the Premier League.

In 2004, Blues announced a proposed 55,000-capacity stadium to replace St. Andrew's.

Those plans would have also seen the introduction of a sports village in the city.

However, the proposals were ultimately shelved, with the club remaining at their existing ground.

Birmingham have played home matches at St. Andrew's since it was opened in 1906.

3 Birmingham plan to move into their new 62,000-stadium by 2030 Credit: BIRMINGHAM CITY FC

The ground was most recently renovated between 2020 and 2023, with the rebuilding of the lower tiers in the Kop and Tilton Road Stands.

This season marks the club's second campaign back in the Championship.

Birmingham secured an immediate return to the second tier in 2025 following their relegation to League One.

Chris Davies' side currently sit tenth after eight matches following a 2-2 draw at home against Middlesbrough on Saturday.

Sports.title: Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute to his mum
Sports.content:
Ronald Koeman Jr breaks down in tears on pitch during emotional tribute to his mum

Ronald Koeman Jr was visibly emotional during a tribute to his late mother during Telstar's match against AZ Alkmaar.

The Eredivisie clash was paused in the 13th minute for an applause in honour of Bartina Koeman.

2 Koeman Jr broke down in tears during a tribute to his late mother Credit: ESPN

Her passing aged 65 was announced on Wednesday following a battle with breast cancer.

Bartina was the wife of former Netherlands captain and manager Ronald Koeman.

Tribute to Bartina Koeman

She was also Koeman Jr's mother, with the goalkeeper on the pitch for Telstar at the time of the tribute.

He could be seen wiping away tears as her picture was displayed on the big screen inside AZ's AFAS Stadion.

Supporters from both clubs paid tribute during the minute's applause.

Meanwhile, Telstar fans held sparklers aloft as they honoured Bartina's life.

Koeman Jr had joined on with the applause before using his shirt to wipe his eyes as he broke down in tears.

As the minute's applause concluded, he clapped the crowd to thank them for their tributes.

AZ went on to win the match 1-0 thanks to Mexx Meerdink's first half goal.

The result leaves Telstar 13th in the Eredivisie standings after seven matches this season.

However, they are now winless in their last six despite Koeman Jr scoring twice against Cambuur earlier this month, becoming the first goalkeeper in Eredivisie history to score two goals in one match.

The 31-year-old was making his first appearance since his mother's death was announced.

Bartina had been married to Koeman for 41 years prior to her passing, with the couple having three children together.

The former Everton manager stepped down as national team boss following their World Cup exit in order to care for her.

Announcing the tragic news on social media, Koeman wrote: "With deep sorrow, but also with great pride and love, we say goodbye to my wonderful wife, our dearest mom and grandma.”

The news also came after Koeman Jr had welcomed the birth of his first child earlier this month.

2 A minute's applause was held in honour of Bartina during AZ's win over Telstar Credit: ESPN

Bartina was first diagnosed with breast cancer back in 2010, from which she recovered after receiving treatment.

Having recovered, the disease returned in 2018 before she was diagnosed with chronic breast cancer two years ago.

Koeman announced last year, though, that the cancer cells had spread.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: Witton Albion's FA Cup dream comes to an end with seven-goal thrashing after defensive crisis... with one centre-half missing on a stag do as Daily Mail Sport's baton passes to South Shields
Sports.content:
FA Cup Second Qualifying Round: South Shields 7 Witton Albion 0

With some degree of difficulty, Witton Albion have requisitioned Accrington Stanley’s bus for the journey to the far north but there’s a misunderstanding about which motorway junction one of their players is to meet it at, and then a 30-minute delay because of a crash on the A19. That leaves only 90 minutes until kick-off when their five-hour journey brings them up to South Shields’ impressive ground, on the Tyneside coast.

The bus has been sourced by Paul Houghton, Witton’s kit man, who everyone calls ‘square’ (‘because of the shape of my head,’ he explains) and though he organises much more than his title suggests, finding ‘a bus with tables’ has proved taxing because there’s apparently a general shortage of them. But it’s the scarcity of central defenders which looks more worrying for the eighth-tier Cheshire team, who we are with for a third round on our journey to Wembley told in 13 instalments, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the team who beat them, all the way to the final.

Both Geffry Ebhote, outstanding at the back when Witton shocked aircraft manufacturing club Avro in the 1st Qualifying Round, and Wade Rutherford have had longstanding social commitments today – one of them is on a stag do – so 35-year-old manager Benny Harrison, an accomplished centre-half in his playing days, has had to name himself a substitute.

When Harrison wanders over to talk after the warm-up, it’s evident that he’s an extremely good man for a challenge like this, against a fully professional team, two leagues above Witton in the pyramid. ‘Last time I played myself, I thought I was going to get sacked and I came on and we won six games in a row!’ he says, with an easy equanimity.

Harrison teaches in a school with special educational needs and in the month or so that we’ve got to know each other, it’s become clear that the challenging classroom role is useful when helping a group of footballers navigate the Northern Premier League, and this mini-Cup run.

‘You learn to understand what sort of individual each of them is,’ Harrison told me, one Thursday night, as he struggled to make himself heard above the noise of Witton Albion Brass Band practising in the room next door.

‘People have everyday lives and something might have happened to affect them and the way they are responding.’ (Witton have had a brass band named after them ever since offering rehearsal room at their stadium to a local bread factory works ensemble who’d lost their practice space.)

Witton Albion's 35-year-old manager Benny Harrison, an accomplished centre-half in his playing days, had to name himself a substitute after his two defenders were unable to play

Witton travelled five hours to reach South Shields' stadium on Tyneside, pitching up at the club only 90 minutes before kick-off

South Shields chairman Geoff Thompson has ambitions to take the club back to the Football League by 2030, after what would be 100 years away

Witton supporters Will and Ben have transported a bass drum all the way to South Shields and, though not members of any band, are making all the noise before kick-off. The club haven’t managed to put a supporters’ coach on so there are barely 50 of their fans here, and people have been telling the Radio Witton volunteer commentators all week that they’ll be tuning into their live broadcast instead. ‘It means we need to be on top of our game,’ says Andrew Nelson, one of them, as he heads anxiously up to the gantry.

Here, in microcosm, is the power of community which is football’s lifeblood at the clubs far from the pomp and ceremony of high-powered sports cars and six-figure weekly salaries. South Shields know all about that priceless commodity, too, despite their £3.4million main stand with 15 corporate boxes, their fully professional playing squad, and promotion ambitions.

Barely a decade ago, the team were playing local Northern League games at Peterlee, 30 miles down the coast, because they couldn’t afford to renew the lease on this ground, which was at risk of being sold to the Port of Tyne as a container park. Geoff Thompson, a local businessman who ran a listed corporate energy consultancy, then stepped in to buy the freehold on the ground and take the club on a remarkable journey which has mirrored the local town's own advance from the depths of post-industrial despair to an attractive tourism destination with sandy beaches.

‘At the start, I wasn’t taking a long-term view,’ says Thompson, the club’s chairman, sitting in a tented dining area which he envisages being the site of a second stand, to go with the main one he has financed, if the club can maintain their upward trajectory. ‘But I think there’s a place for a club like us. We used to be in the old Second Division and in 2030 it will be 100 years since we fell out of the Football League. We think we could return there and that League 2, or even League 1, would be a good position for us. It would be wonderful to achieve that around 100 years on.’

After four league titles in 11 years under his shrewd ownership, there is belief in the potential around this place. That was equally evident when Thompson, sensing the need to begin passing on the baton after a cancer diagnosis and successful surgery, engaged a firm of Newcastle financial consultants to draw up an ‘information memorandum’ and begin the search for new investors. Four months ago, an international consortium led by Jason Ye, a New York-based capital markets lawyer, and including equity partners from Singapore and Shanghai, took a 75 per cent ownership of the club, with Thompson, who maintains a 23per cent share, still very much present. Fans own the rest.

Barely a decade ago, South Shields were playing local Northern League games at Peterlee, 30 miles down the coast, because they couldn’t afford to renew the lease on this ground

South Shields' Paul Blackett (centre), a non-league legend in these parts, scored twice

Witton Albion players commiserate with the 50 or so fans who made the long journey

Home fans enjoy some sweets from Kets 'n' Pop

Financially, it all feels a world away from Witton, with their ownership structure of 400 registered shareholders and stipulation that no one may own more than 10 per cent, which has left them dependent on generous benefactors. South Shields’ club shop is selling £45 framed images of striker Paul Blackett and £55 replica training tops. You don’t find those at a seventh-tier club.

Money offers no guarantees. South Shields lost 6-0 at league leaders Hereford the previous weekend and US-owned Hartlepool United will part company with their manager before this day is done. But the chasm between the sides is immediately obvious as Shields capitalise on their opponents’ depleted defence to go 3-0 up in 12 minutes.

Blackett, a non-league legend in these parts, scores two of them but Liverpool-born Sean McGurk, signed from Swindon Town last year, is the prime talent, creating two and almost bending in one of his own. Witton’s Freddy Garbutt enters the picture, with excellent close control for a 6ft 6in striker, but Blackett runs through to make it 4-0 by half-time.

Motivational talk is hard when the game has gone so early. Harrison tells his players to find some intensity, leave everything out on the field, but Shields do not relent. Northern Ireland international Jordan Jones runs much of a second half in which Cedwyn Evans scores twice and 31-year-old Adam Campbell, a teenage player for Newcastle United in Europe at the age of 15, wraps things up.

JOURNEY TO WEMBLEY, SO FAR

Extra preliminary round, August 8: Nelson 3-2 Stockport Georgians Preliminary round, August 22: Witton Albion 1-0 Nelson 1st qualifying round, September 5: Avro 0-2 Witton Albion 2nd qualifying round, September 19: South Shields 7-0 Witton Albion

It seems symbolic that Campbell wears No27 and Scott is No19. Our Journey to Wembley is entering the world of substantial squads and you suspect Witton will be the last on the journey to line 1 to 11. But there’s still an unmistakable sense of community about this place, epitomised by the little sweet shop, Kets N’ Pop, run by a couple advanced in years, Helen and Mark, under the old Clock Stand. ‘Kets’ is local vernacular for ‘sweets.’ They press a £1 packet of bonbons on me. 'No charge!'

The final whistle is a mercy for Witton, whose race in this tournament is certainly run. ‘We were never going to win the FA Cup and this match won’t define our season,’ says Harrison, as he heads back to a hectic domestic life in which his three-month-old daughter features substantially. ‘It’s a lonely place on the pitch when you’re up against it like that but we didn’t throw in the towel.’

We may also be leaving behind the last side on our journey who head across the pitch at full-time to shake the hands of virtually every travelling fan before leaving the pitch. Standing there to greet Witton's players are drummers Will and Ben, whose rhythm understandably tailed off at 4-0. ‘We’re proud of the boys,’ says Ben, hauling the drum to his Toyota Yaris for the long drive home.

Sports.title: Fuming Alvaro Arbeloa accuses Premier League referees of 'not wanting Man United to lose' - claiming 'EVERY decision' went their way in last-gasp draw against Fulham
Sports.content:
Fuming Alvaro Arbeloa accuses Premier League referees of 'not wanting Man United to lose' - claiming 'EVERY decision' went their way in last-gasp draw against Fulham

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa's furious rant is set to land him an FA sanction after he claimed officials 'would not let Man United lose' during Sunday's 1-1 draw.

The Cottagers looked set to see out a famous win over United until Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike salvaged a barely-deserved point for Michael Carrick's side.

At the heart of Arbeloa's annoyance was the fact that he felt the foul awarded to United, adjudged on Harry Maguire, 35 seconds before Cunha scored was unjust and ultimately cost Fulham three points.

In his immediate post-match comments, Arbeloa could barely contain his anger.

'Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they would not let Man Utd lose. We deserved a little bit more,' Arbeloa said.

'We were so, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

'We knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referee has been doing in all the matches, so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.'

Alvaro Arbeloa claimed that match officials 'did not want Man United to lose' on Sunday

Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike cost Fulham three points, leaving Arbeloa fuming

Perhaps there had been a word in Arbeloa's ear before his post-match press conference with journalists as he looked to tone down his criticism.

'My English is not so good,' Arbeloa said.

'Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.'

Arbeloa's initial rant will almost certainly land him in hot water with the FA as questioning the integrity of match officials or alleging bias is a surefire way to land a hefty fine, or even touchline ban.

Former Fulham boss Marco Silva fell foul of this rule previously, as have many of Arbeloa's peers.

The result, while not a precious win, is still a step in the right direction for Fulham, who lifted themselves off the foot of the table, condemning Tottenham Hotspur to last place for the first time since 2009.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling vows to be 'better than yesterday' as former England footballer, 31, breaks his silence after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession following £270,000 Lamborghini car crash
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling says he is seeking 'progress over perfection' after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession.

In his first Instagram post since bodycam footage of his May arrest was released, Sterling says his goal is to 'be better than yesterday'.

On Tuesday, Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini while driving under the influence of laughing gas.

Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with the drug after submitting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90 minutes of dangerous driving, in which he zig-zagged on the M25 and M3 motorways before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate.

The 31-year-old former England international was arrested by police who claim he tried to hide nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, from them by moving it to the back seat of his black Lamborghini Urus SUV.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap. An officer can be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He can then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Raheem Sterling says he is seeking 'progress over perfection' following his court case

Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini in May

The 31-year-old was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after swerving his car on the M25 and M3

Sterling is asked 'can you jump out for me' and who was at the wheel at the time of the crash, but does not reply.

The officer adds: 'So you refuse to answer, okay.'

Sterling is told to get out of the car, asked his name and age at the roadside and to 'put the phone down, stop playing games. Stop tensing up.'

The former Manchester City and Chelsea star, who won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 2018-19, is then read his rights as he is arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange on the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his football career at Dutch club Feyenoord. He remains without a club.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28. Police found six cannisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting. Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling

The former England international was pictured arriving in court today to face charges following a car crash in May

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said. Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone.'

Evidence presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon.'

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes, saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents. For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave from inside to outside lane and back and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

It was after Sterling had left the M3 near Farnborough, Hampshire, hit the gate and come to halt with the tyres of his wheels ripped up, that police found him sitting in T-shirt and shorts in the passenger seat of the car.

One officer told him to 'stop tensing up' after he had stepped out of the car. Sterling replied: 'I'm not tensing up.' Sterling provided breath tests, which established he was not under the influence of cannabis, cocaine or alcohol. But he later refused requests for a blood test, insisting that a lawyer of his choosing must be present, having rejected the offer of a duty solicitor. He also refused to answer any police questions.

Mr Jones said of Sterling's conduct: 'He was attempting to impose a condition on provision of a specimen. He was told the investigation could not be delayed for that reason. At the roadside, there was cooperation without the need for legal advice. When the search for the presence of drugs started, the cooperation ended.'

Sterling's barrister, Jason Bartfeld QC, told the court that there was 'extensive personal mitigation' in his case and that the footballer had taken 'voluntary steps to mitigate his difficulties.'

Mr Bartfeld agreed that this was a 'top category case' because it was a prolonged period of dangerous driving and Sterling was suffering 'serious impairment'. But he said the nitrous oxide would only have caused impairment in 'short periods' and that the chemical did not pose the same risks as cannabis or alcohol.

He claimed police had left Sterling confused about the blood sample. Sterling later told police in a statement: 'I asked for a solicitor. I did not fully understand I had not slept all night and was tired and confused.'

Sterling could face a maximum two years' imprisonment. The case was adjourned until November for pre-sentencing reports.

Sports.title: Furious Gary Neville rips into Man United's 'walking' stars and tells Michael Carrick to STOP defending them after 'absolutely pathetic' draw with Fulham: 'Worst 15 minutes I've EVER seen'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville branded Manchester United’s lack of effort ‘an absolute disgrace’ after their insipid 1-1 draw against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

Matheus Cunha’s deflected effort in the 89th minute rescued United from a third defeat in a week, but even the Brazilian admitted that his team didn’t try hard enough.

United go into the international break in 12th place with five points – their joint-lowest total after five games of the season in the Premier League era.

Former United defender Neville fumed on Sky Sports: ‘I rarely say teams don't make an effort because that's the ultimate criticism. That first 15 minutes of the second half, and generally the first 60 minutes, United were an absolute disgrace.

‘I’ve watched Man United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen. Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort.

‘There needs to be a reset in terms of structure. They don't want to do the ugly part of the game.

Gary Neville branded Manchester United an 'absolute disgrace' for their perceived lack of effort during their 1-1 draw with Fulham

Michael Carrick defended his men, who have made the joint-worst start to a season in the club's Premier League history

‘I've never seen a Manchester United team walk as much as that. Michael (Carrick) needs to stop defending them.

'If they carry on like that, they will concede so many goals week after week. They were lucky to concede one.

'I just see apathy and ambling around the pitch. They can all work harder than that- they're getting outrun in every match.'

After Cunha scored a late equaliser – heavily deflected off David Affengruber – to cancel out a disastrous own-goal by team-mate Lisandro Martinez, the forward admitted that United only woke up once Fulham went ahead.

‘In the second half it was like they put in more energy than us,’ he said. ‘We cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding a goal, and it cannot be like this.’

In United's defence, they came up against an inspired goalkeeper in Bernd Leno, who made five saves and won man of the match.

Lisandro Martinez, Bryan Mbeumo, and Marcus Rashford were all denied by the German, while Bruno Fernandes and Cunha hit the post.

Fulham's opener was unfortunate but not undeserved, as Calvin Bassey's shot comically deflected in off Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens.

Manchester United had 25 shots but were accused of lacking defensive effort by Neville

Goalscorer Matheus Cunha admitted that Fulham had 'more energy' than the Red Devils

Carrick attempted to defend his men at full time, telling Sky Sports: 'We should have won the game, we created enough. We had a lot of good play. The goal that we did concede is one of them goals.

'The boys could've thought it was one of those days and that it went against us, but I really liked the reaction. We nearly won it at the end.

'We came to get the win, the way the game has panned out and the reaction is the positive we take from it.

'Their goalkeeper, the saves that he's made, he's made three top saves, arguably man of the match. That tells you how much we worked him. We hit the post twice and had a lot of opportunities. There's things to take from it.

'I don't think we were (passive). Do you think we were passive?'

Told that his team didn't have any shots in the first 15 minutes of the second half, he hit back: 'That doesn't mean we were passive. It's the Premier League, you're going to have spells where you don't have it all your own way.'

Asked if he was satisfied with his team's energy levels, Carrick said: 'Yeah.'

He added: 'We can take a lot and learn a lot from today. We need to be better and we will be.'

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa was denied his first Premier League win, and accused referee Peter Bankes of favouring United.

‘There were so many things for them,’ said Arbeloa. ‘Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they (referees) don't like Manchester United to lose.

‘We were so, so close to our first victory that we are a little bit upset now.’

Sports.title: Celtic supporters' bus bursts into FLAMES: Emergency services rush to scene in Glasgow to evacuate fans after Old Firm derby
Sports.content:
Celtic supporters' bus bursts into FLAMES: Emergency services rush to scene in Glasgow to evacuate fans after Old Firm derby

A group of football fans suffered a major scare as their coach went up in flames following Sunday's Old Firm derby.

As frustrated Celtic fans headed for home having seen their side lose 1-0 at Parkhead to their bitterest rivals Rangers, the biggest concern of the day was still to come.

As a group of Celtic fans travelled home the rear of their coach caught fire on the A728 near to the Emirates Arena.

Thick black smoke soon dominated the Glasgow sky as fans were quickly evacuated and moved to safety as emergency services rushed to the scene in the east end of the city.

Police Scotland have confirmed nobody was injured.

But in a latest twist, McLean's Coaches, who own, the coach, believe 'vandalism' caused the fire.

A group of Celtic fans were evacuated as their coach home burst into flames after the match

A statement from McLean's Coaches, shared by the Daily Record, after the fire claimed: 'We are aware of an incident involving one of our coaches on the Clyde Gateway earlier today. Based on the initial information and images we have received, we have reason to believe the incident may have been caused by vandalism.

'The matter has been reported to the relevant authorities, who are investigating the circumstances. The vehicle has been recovered and will undergo a full inspection.'

Two fire engines were seen on site with the Clyde Gateway brought to a standstill as the blaze was tackled and eventually halted with stunned fans watching on from the side of the road.

It marked the end to a disappointing day for those rooting for Celtic after they were narrowly beaten.

Ryan Naderi's first half strike was enough by the time the final whistle sounded as Celtic's misery was compounded by the fact that they have now lost to Rangers twice in the space of eight days.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher insists £116m Liverpool star Florian Wirtz must be DROPPED by Andoni Iraola after his 'poorest performance' in a Reds shirt against Bournemouth
Sports.content:
