Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped by Liverpool after 'one of his poorest' performances in a red shirt at Bournemouth.

The £116million attacker has flattered to deceive since pitching up from Bayer Leverkusen and Liverpool legend Carragher was left totally unimpressed with his showing on the south coast.

'That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt,' Carragher, said, speaking on the new Jamie Carragher Podcast.

'I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

'But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.'

Carragher's comments laid bare just how little Wirtz has done to convince of his talents in England, with the Sky pundit adding that he simply doesn't see 'how he's going to hurt' teams.

Florian Wirtz (left) needs to be dropped when Liverpool face Man City, says Jamie Carragher

Wirtz (right) once again struggled to exert any influence when Liverpool faced Bournemouth

'The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there,' Carragher added as part of his damning assessment.

'Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

'And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't.'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola now goes into a three-week international break with plenty ponder ahead of a return to action against league leaders Manchester City on October 11.

'I think going forward Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team,' Carragher added.

'I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn't produce [against Bournemouth], he's then going to have a three-week break.

'By the time we come back, we're into October. Before you know it, it'll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it'll feel like we're getting to Christmas. He has to do something!

'Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team.'

Sports.title: How Led Zeppelin-loving anglophile from Los Angeles, who worships Jeremy Clarkson, beat Rory McIlroy to land PGA title, as Spanish outsider chokes to miss out on £1.3m prize
Sports.content:
How Led Zeppelin-loving anglophile from Los Angeles, who worships Jeremy Clarkson, beat Rory McIlroy to land PGA title, as Spanish outsider chokes to miss out on £1.3m prize

For JJ Spaun, the Led Zeppelin-loving anglophile from Los Angeles, there was a fairway to heaven at the BMW Championship. For Rory McIlroy, a resident on the Wentworth estate, there was a near miss and a short journey home to process it.

Whatever difficulties McIlroy is experiencing with his swing, he was sufficiently grooved to card a 68 and a 15-under-par finish that left the world No2 two strokes behind Spaun.

If there were frustrations about his proximity to victory, then they were nothing compared to the plight of Manuel Elvira. Heard of him? If you hadn’t then that would make most of us.

Ranked 296th in the world, and without a win of any description in his eight years as a professional, the Spaniard, 30, had the DP World Tour’s flagship event in the palm of his hands. And then he suffered one of those gut-squeezing chokes that crop up in this maddening game.

His dramas came on the fairway of the 18th hole, a par five, where he stood at 17 under par. His drive had left 228 yards to the front of the green and this hole had been a birdie-fest all week. With Spaun already in the clubhouse, a par would have guaranteed Elvira a play-off; a four would be worth £1.3million and more than the rest of his journeyman career combined.

What followed was somewhat soul destroying. Having made the nervy decision to lay-up short of the creek, Elvira committed the cardinal sin of missing the fairway and finding a bunker. From there, it got so much worse – he flew his recovery to the foot of the 18th grandstand, where his ball nearly hit a group of journalists, and Elvira then proceeded to duff his fourth into another bunker.

On his victory, Spaun said: ‘It means so much. I've kind of blossomed into this player I never thought I could be'

JJ Spaun's wife Melody accompanied his final round with a Jeremy Clarkson mask on a stick

Rory McIroy's second place means he is only just behind Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai

By the time his ball disappeared below ground, after his seventh stroke, the series of blunders had cost him around £800,000. A cheque of approximately £500,000 for a share of second place with McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Adam Scott is nothing to be sniffed at, but the tears of his wife at greenside told their own story.

His reaction after signing for a 70: ‘Devastated.’

The spoils instead went to a man who admitted he was playing with a ‘chip on my shoulder’. That was Spaun, the 2025 US Open champion who recently incurred the surprise indignity of being left out of the American team for the Presidents Cup.

Channelling his energies on a trip to Surrey, the late-blooming 36-year-old made his point emphatically with this performance – his closing 67 started with a bogey and not a single blemish followed. Finishing with four birdies in his final five holes, he sealed the deal in style.

That it occurred in England was notable for the fact he is besotted with this country. He and his wife regularly spend holidays in the Cotswolds and more recently he has become addicted to watching Clarkson’s Farm on Amazon Prime – his wife Melody accompanied his final round with a Jeremy Clarkson mask on the end of a stick. Each to their own.

On his victory, Spaun said: ‘It means so much. I've kind of blossomed into this player I never thought I could be. England is a place that's dear to my family's heart and the stars kind of aligned this week for me to come out on top.’

Detailing the Clarkson infatuation, Spaun added: ‘We've grown fond of him, along with the English culture. We take holidays in December in the Cotswolds, and we really enjoy his show. I went to his pub, The Farmer's Dog, with the hopes to catch a glimpse of him but he wasn't around.

‘My wife said we would have a surprise guest following us this week if I competed in the tournament and sure enough on Friday morning I saw the face of Jeremy Clarkson and her holding it. Jeremy was there in spirit and I think he brought me good fortune.’

Golf is nothing if not utterly mystifying. In McIlroy’s case, that extends to understanding his swing, which he warned might take five or six months to fix but looked pretty handy here. His tie for second place means he is only marginally behind Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai standings for the final two months of the season. If McIlroy can pass the American, he will win the order of merit for an eighth time, equalling Colin Montgomerie.

‘I had my chances out there,’ McIlroy said. ‘I putted OK for the most part this week but I missed a lot of putts. I wish I had some of those putts back but I have to be encouraged with where my game is at.

‘I hit the ball really well today and I’m encouraged with the signs. I just have to keep working at it.

‘I have three events until the end of my DP World Tour season. I'm not sure what Patrick's schedule looks like coming up, but I feel like I have enough opportunities. It would be obviously amazing to match Monty's record.’

Sports.title: Only a late stroke of luck spared dismal Man United defeat at struggling Fulham, but it's Sir Jim Ratcliffe - not Michael Carrick - who must take the blame for his club's worsening crisis, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Only a late stroke of luck spared dismal Man United defeat at struggling Fulham, but it's Sir Jim Ratcliffe - not Michael Carrick - who must take the blame for his club's worsening crisis, writes OLIVER HOLT

There is a pub on Fulham High Street called The Eight Bells.

Paper signs on the windows say that it is reserved for away fans only and on Sunday afternoon, the strains of Manchester United supporters singing in support of their team drifted into the afternoon sunshine before the game.

It is reputed to be Fulham's oldest pub. In fact, there are unsubstantiated claims it is even older than United's back-four. It might have been more appropriate if it was called The Seven Bells, because that is what United got knocked out of them for much of their clash with Alvaro Arbeloa's side at Craven Cottage.

They were outplayed for long periods of the match but escaped with a 1-1 draw after a stroke of luck in the dying minutes brought them a last-gasp equaliser.

They salvaged a little pride but not much. They have five points from their opening five games against Hull City, Ipswich Town, Everton, Manchester City and Fulham.

A season that began with some hopes of them challenging for the title has collapsed into a situation where they are 10 points behind Manchester City before we have even entered the last week of September. Sir Jim Ratcliffe, their minority owner, is an expert on once great things now 'on the slide'. He has added United to his portfolio.

Manchester United are facing more questions than answers after a 1-1 draw away at Fulham

Michael Carrick watched on in dismay as his side looked second best away against Fulham

'It is quite difficult to see how we arrest it,' Sir Jim said of the UK's travails. That sounds like a dispiritingly familiar refrain to United fans.

It is 13 years since they last won the Premier League title and it will be 14 in May. They are too far behind City and Arsenal already to have any chance of ending their drought.

They had some momentum coming into this campaign. Now they have none.

Manager Michael Carrick will get some of the blame for that but this is not his fault. The horror show that is unfolding now is the fault of Sir Jim and his band of hapless executives who masterminded a dreadful summer transfer window that has left United hopelessly adrift of their rivals.

Knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton last week, spurned by the greatest of their young talents, JJ Gabriel, and at war with their own supporters, United had chances and hit the woodwork twice but they looked more predictable and more weary than Fulham.

This was a Fulham, by the way, that were bottom of the table at the start of play but looked more imaginative, more optimistic, more youthful and more coherent than their opponents.

Fulham's point took them above Tottenham Hotspur, who will spend the three weeks of the international break rooted to the foot of the division.

United had spent the first few minutes of the game chasing lengthening shadows. Fulham played the ball about confidently and patiently. They evaded United's half-hearted attempts to press them until a ball was fizzed in to Gonzalo Garcia on the edge of the United box. Garcia snatched at his shot and dragged it wide but it was a chastening start for the visitors.

Lisandro Martinez deflected the ball past a helpless Senne Lammens in the Man United goal

Calvin Bassey wheeled away in celebration after his initial strike eventually led to the first goal

It was a tough watch for Manchester United's travelling fans, who saw a side devoid of energy

When United finally established a foothold in the game, they nearly took the lead. Lisandro Martinez ran on to a loose ball and hit a dipping swerving shot from 25 yards that was destined for the top corner until Bernd Leno launched himself through the air and tipped it wide.

United came close again midway through the half. Matheus Cunha stole the ball away from a Fulham defender as he tried to shepherd it out of play and pulled the ball back for Bruno Fernandes.

Fernandes clipped it towards goal but the ball rolled against the foot of Leno's right-hand post and dribbled away to safety.

United had made the best chances but Fulham had been the better team.

That dynamic shifted after half an hour when Garcia had a golden chance to put Fulham ahead but miskicked in front of goal as he tried to convert Alex Iwobi's cross. Lammens saved well when Sander Berge tried to convert the loose ball.

Then it was the turn of Josh King to go close. King should have been included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad after an outstanding start to this season but was overlooked. Everything about his play in this match showed why he should have been picked.

Fifteen minutes before half-time, he jinked past Luke Shaw with ease and rifled in a shot that Lammens kept out with his right boot.

In the midst of Fulham's missed chances, United hit the woodwork again. Cunha's shot from the edge of the area deflected off a defender and spun up into the air. It was looping over Leno until the goalkeeper got a hand to it and touched it on to the post. United were being outplayed but they were always in the game.

A minute before the break, Marcus Rashford volleyed over from ten yards out. At the other end, King went past Maguire and fell to the ground as Maguire's arm brushed him on his way through.

It was not a foul but nor was it the yellow card that referee Peter Bankes brandished at King.

Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike ensured Manchester United left with something

The second half started slowly but exploded into life just after the hour. Calvin Bassey wrestled the ball away from Cunha on the edge of the United box and unleashed a fierce left-foot drive. Lammens blocked it with his left leg but the ball rebounded to Martinez.

The Argentina defender could not react quickly enough to control it and it bounced off him and back towards goal. Lammens tried to clear it but got his feet in a tangle and deflected it into his own net. Martinez turned away in dismay.

United thought they had equalised minutes later. Bryan Mbeumo curled a shot goalwards and began to wheel away to celebrate before Leno pulled off a magnificent, flying one-handed save that preserved Fulham's lead.

United dominated possession after that but showed little in the way of cutting edge. It took a slice of fortune to drag them level. Fulham held on until two minutes from the end but then Cunha cut in from the left and fired in a shot. Leno had it covered but it deflected off David Affengruber's outstretched foot and bobbled apologetically over the line.

Sports.title: Luke Littler's bid for darts history goes up in smoke with shock defeat to rival
Sports.content:
Luke Littler's bid for darts history goes up in smoke with shock defeat to rival

Darts star Luke Littler was gunning for a PDC major clean sweep but saw his efforts halted in emphatic fashion by Johnny Clayton in Amsterdam on Sunday evening

View 2 Images Luke Littler has seen his dreams of a PDC major clean sweep slip away (Image: Getty Images)

Luke Littler saw his hopes of a PDC major clean sweep ruined after being thumped by Johnny Clayton at the World Series of Darts. The 19-year-old took on Clayton at the quarter-final stage of the competition.

‌



And despite having opportunities to seal 10 leg victories, Littler only managed to finish off four of those and eventually slipped to defeat, with his Welsh opponent sealing a 10-4 success to progress to the last four.

‌



Clayton said: “I thought, go out relax and try your best. He wasn’t full flowing there. You have to take your chances.

‌



“Luke missed a lot of darts on doubles on outs. That’s the name of the game. You have to take your chances and I did that today somehow.

Furious Luke Littler threatens major boycott after abuse at World Series of Darts Finals READ MORE :

“The last dart on a double hurts. Whoever you play against it puts pressure on the player. All due respect to Luke, fantastic.

“That last leg he missed, missed, missed. I thought ‘oh my God’. He just gave me chances after chances. That’s not the Luke Littler that we all know. Jonny Clayton can play darts as well. Loved it.

‌



“I’ve had enough experience against Luke in the Premier League. I know what he’s about, he knows what I’m about. We play darts, nothing else. We try and keep the crowd happy and play our best. It was my night, that’s all it is.”

The defeat was certainly a shock to Littler, who had not found himself on the losing side of a major since his defeat to James Wade in the European Championship last October. Since then, he had won the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League and World Matchplay and was aiming to become the first darts player to secure victory in each of the majors in the same season.

View 2 Images Littler was eliminated by Johnny Clayton (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Littler’s defeat to Clayton also rounded off a difficult tournament, where he had received a less-than-warm welcome from the Dutch crowd once again. Speaking earlier in the tournament, he threatened not to return.

Littler said: “If the Dutch stay like this, then I’m not going to do any Euro tours over there. There’s just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I’m getting booed. Just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.”

Meanwhile, Raymond van Barneveld suggested that the world champion might have succumbed to the pressure of completing a perfect season. He said: "It's the pressure. Everyone talks about: 'Can he do the whole year and win all the big majors.' It gives big pressure. He wants to perform, and he's the best player at the moment, but everyone is fallible.

Article continues below

"Everyone wants your scalp, and Jonny Clayton did it perfectly today. In all honestly, Littler missed some crucial shots. Everyone thought Littler would win the whole event, but now it's really open for all four players left."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick denies Gary Neville claim in staunch defence of Man Utd stars
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick denies Gary Neville claim in staunch defence of Man Utd stars

Manchester United have endured a poor start to Michael Carrick's first full season at the helm but the Red Devils boss has come out fighting with his assessment of his side's performance

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Manchester United have endured a poor start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick insisted Manchester United can still have a “big season” after Gary Neville branded the performance “absolutely pathetic.”

‌



Matheus Cunha’s deflected shot snatched a last-minute draw but the result drew stinging criticism from Sky pundit Neville as United go into the international break languishing in 12th place.

‌



Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, whose side gained a point to leave Tottenham rock bottom, could also find himself trouble with the FA after claiming refs “don’t like Manchester United to lose” as he was upset with some of Peter Bankes’ decisions.

‌



Neville was very critical on Sky about the way United played at the start of the second half and said: “I've watched Man United since the age of five. That's the worst 15 minutes I've seen them play. Absolutely pathetic.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But Carrick, whose side are already ten points behind leaders Manchester City, said: “There’s still a big season ahead. It’s a long season and this is part of the journey.

“I’m not playing it down - we wanted more points. I understand the frustration. But what bothers me is that we want better results.

“We want more points, we're going to have a spell where it's not quite going for you and we've had a spell of that where small things have ended up as big things.

‌



“We don't think things are perfect by any means. We need to win football matches. The supporters were top-drawer again today and we have to give them something to keep shouting about.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has given his verdict on Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

“I think we did enough to win the game. I think we could win it. I was pleased with how we responded, the boys kept their belief and kept doing the right things. I think a point is the least we should take.”

‌



Carrick was also asked about Neville's comments and if his side were 'too passive' at Craven Cottage but claimed that he did not share that verdict.

He said: "I didn't think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It's the Premier League and you will have spells where you don't have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don't think anyone gets that in this league."

He added: "I think we can take a lot from today. I think we can learn a lot as well. We can be better at certain things, that is pretty clear, but there were some god signs today."

Sports.title: Furious Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa claims referees 'don't like Man Utd to lose'
Sports.content:
Furious Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa claims referees 'don't like Man Utd to lose'

Fulham are still without their first Premier League win under new boss Alvaro Arbeloa after being pegged back late on by Manchester United at Craven Cottage on Sunday afternoon

View 2 Images Alvaro Arbeloa was far from happy after Fulham's draw with Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Alvaro Arbeloa sensationally claimed referees 'don't like' Manchester United losing after Fulham's late draw. The Londoners looked on their way to their first Premier League victory under the Spanish coach.

‌



Lisandro Martinez had put through his own net to give Fulham the lead, only for Matheus Cunha's late deflected effort to ensure a share of the points.

‌



And while Arbeloa bemoaned his side's fortune for not being able to hold out for a much-needed win, he also took aim at the referees for not awarding a foul by Harry Maguire just seconds before United's equaliser.

‌



Arbeloa said: "We were so, so close. We were a little unlucky again but we know it was going to be difficult against a big team and we have seen what the referee has been doing through the match.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don't like Manchester United to lose.

"We were so, so close to our first victory that we are a little bit upset now. I think we did a good game.

"Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

‌



"We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

View 2 Images Alvaro Arbeloa was left furious at the referee following Fulham's draw with Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

"Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland.

Article continues below

"Now we have an October that will be so important for us. We have shown the team we want to be and if we play in this way the victories will come."

Arbeloa now has a few weeks to stew on Fulham’s failure to secure victory against United, with the Premier League due to take a break due to the first international window of the season. Their next opportunity for victory is set to come in three weeks’ time as they take on newly-promoted Ipswich.

Sports.title: Premier League propose big Carabao Cup change in £1.8bn 'new deal for football'
Sports.content:
Premier League propose big Carabao Cup change in £1.8bn 'new deal for football'

The Premier League are offering the English Football League a 'new deal for football' worth £1.8billion, but they now want one massive change to the Carabao Cup

View 2 Images Premier League clubs wants changes to the Carabao Cup semi-finals (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

The Premier League reportedly want Carabao Cup semi-final ties to be decided over one match rather than two as part of a 'new deal for football'. A proposed agreement with the English Football League is said to effectively double the existing solidarity payment, which is divided among clubs across all three EFL divisions, to £1.8billion.

‌



It would be spread across 10 seasons, and both leagues are reportedly around £27million apart in negotiations. However, there is growing confidence of an agreement.

‌



Premier League clubs have unanimously approved the proposal. EFL sides doing likewise would avoid any involvement by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

‌



Andros Townsend delivers perfect response after being run over by pitch roller in freak accident READ MORE :

Richarlison takes to social media with clear message after Tottenham lose again READ MORE :

The Daily Mail reports that another condition of their additional funding would be to progress talks with the National League over new clubs earning League Two promotion every season. They cite sources that claim the Premier League wants to reduce its reliance on ownership funding for EFL clubs.

Controls on how these funds are spent are proposed, including a stop on any increases in player wages. The proposition also requires 15% of the funds to go towards infrastructure.

It also features a 'lifeboat fund' for clubs entering administration in future. They would be loaned £20million to continue paying essential creditors and operating.

‌



View 2 Images The Carabao Cup semi-finals could stopping being two-legged ties (Image: Paul Currie/Shutterstock)

The EFL want a tweak to their current divisional split of 80:12:8 between the Championship, League One and League Two. Despite the Premier League seeking no change, a change to 75:15:10 is being sought.

Under the new split, based on a mid-table finish, Championship clubs would receive £8.5million more, rising from £12.1million to £20.6million. That translates to a £1.3million uplift in League One, up from £2.5million to £3.8million, whereas League Two payments would grow by £700k, from £1.8million to £2.5million. A 2% increase in the Premier League transfer levy is to cover the increase, which would go from 4% to 6%.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The deal is around 17.5% of what all top-flight clubs earn from their collective broadcast rights. That is 6.5% more than the current level, but half of what the EFL initially sought.

EFL clubs were told about the proposal last week. They will make the final decision once it is ready for the league's board to recommend.

Article continues below

The deal has already been under discussion for six weeks now. It is said that the EFL prefers to wait until the IFR's State of the Game report, which is due to be published by them on 12 October.

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha makes worrying Man Utd admission after Fulham draw - 'We cannot accept this'
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha makes worrying Man Utd admission after Fulham draw - 'We cannot accept this'

Manchester United's inconsistent start to the season continued against Fulham on Sunday evening with Matheus Cunha popping up late on to salvage a draw at Craven Cottage

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha speaks after Man Utd's draw with Fulham

Matheus Cunha slammed his Manchester United teammates for not working as hard as Fulham in their draw at Craven Cottage. The Red Devils looked to be on their way to another defeat on Sunday afternoon after Lisandro Martinez had put through his own net.

‌



Brazilian forward Cunha popped up late on the steal a late draw, albeit it leaves United with just five points from their opening five games of the season - their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign ever.

‌



Giving his assessment, Cunha claimed that United were outworked by their hosts. Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “So frustrating for us because I feel like in the beginning we put the ball in and created some chances.

‌



"We didn’t score, unlucky, and they scored in like one action that’s hard to explain. A lot of luck. Then you come back and this is frustrating because I feel to be honest after we conceding the goal we played much better with a lot of enthusiasm and effort. It’s only one point. We try to never play for one point.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He added: “It’s hard to explain. I feel like after the first half we played well. It was how we planned to do it in the beginning of the second half. I feel like they put more into it than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding a goal but it cannot be like this."

Asked what has to change to get the side back on track, Cunha said: “I have to be honest today I don’t feel like it was about the final decision. We were a bit unlucky. I hit the post. Bruno hit the post. We had other chances. We need to create more and then it will come to us and then we will score more goals.

"Everything we can do to help the team, it's acceptable. When I have the ball, it is not that much difference. Of course we need to improve in every single position. If there is something I can do to help, I will do it."

‌



View 2 Images Cunha scored late on at Craven Cottage (Image: Getty Images)

United's draw at Craven Cottage leaves them with just one win and in 12th in the Premier League. Despite being left frustrated, Cunha has assured that there is still plenty of time for the side to turn things around.

He said: "To be honest, I don't think about outside. I always try to help my teammates. I feel very priviliged to play in this role. It is only the beginning. Last season, there was a lot of noise about and we finished third."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism

Jamie Carragher was critical of Florian Wirtz's performance against Bournemouth, but Andoni Iraola reckons that he made the difference for Liverpool in the second half

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola was left pleased with Florian Wirtz (Image: aspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has praised Florian Wirtz for his second-half turnaround which helped Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0. The Reds claimed all three points at the Vitality Stadium, with Alexander Isak scoring the decisive goal.

‌



But it wasn't going Liverpool's way in the first half, with Wirtz in particular struggling to have a positive impact on the game. That was when Jamie Carragher singled out the £116million signing, saying: "Wirtz has been really poor again. It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all.

‌



"In the main, people have been understanding of his situation. He's new to the league and Liverpool were poor last season. When you come for that price tag, people want goals and assists."

‌



In the second period, the 23-year-old was more lively and played a part in Isak's goal, drawing James Hill out to give his team-mate space to finish. But when Wirtz was subbed off in the 73rd minute, Carragher brutally said that he could have 'no complaints'.

Iraola, though, believes that the German ultimately helped Liverpool win the match, telling Sky Sports: "He started the game slowly, I agree. The first minute they went quite intense and we were not quite with us.

"The duels in the middle. After that first phase, I think we improved. Florian has helped us also to improve.

"Second half he was playing much better, he was finding better spots to receive and turn. Probably we haven't found the last part or moment to score but I think I'm much more happy with his second half than his first one."

‌

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz was criticised by Jamie Carragher against Bournemouth (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Iraola added: "I'm obviously happy with the result. I know it's a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points.

‌



"We could see in the game, at the beginning in the first 20 minutes, we weren't at the level at the game, and it has cost us until afterwards, where we finished the first half better.

"The second half we played better. But that beginning of the game kind of - not surprised us because we knew where we were coming to - but it was difficult for us.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher branded Florian Wirtz 'really poor' in the first half (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"We could see a bit later when Bournemouth started to get tired that in the second half we controlled the game much better. We even had chances to finish but didn't score the second one. But that first part of the game, we were not winning duels, second balls and when they play with this intensity, you have to be at their level."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick explains Benjamin Sesko absence vs Fulham as Man Utd suffer fresh blow
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick explains Benjamin Sesko absence vs Fulham as Man Utd suffer fresh blow

Benjamin Sesko didn't travel with the Manchester United squad for their Premier League clash with Fulham and Michael Carrick has confirmed the reason for his absence

View 2 Images Manchester United were without Benjamin Sesko at Fulham (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are assessing Benjamin Sesko after the striker picked up an injury, Michael Carrick has confirmed. Sesko, 23, missed Sunday's clash with Fulham, having not travelled to London with the rest of Carrick's squad.

‌



The Slovenia international was subbed off in the second half of Wednesday's woeful 3-2 loss at home to Brighton in the Carabao Cup. It's possible that the setback is a reoccurrence of the shin injury which he first sustained during a clash with Liverpool in May and ruled him out of pre-season.

‌



When asked for an update before kick-off at Craven Cottage, Carrick replied: "A little bit of an assessment at the moment. He pulled up after the game the other day with a little bit of pain, so we'll have to see how he is."

‌



Sesko featured in United's first six matches of the season, starting two. He scored in games against Everton and Sabah.

Sesko is now a doubt for his country's Nations League fixtures against Scotland, North Macedonia and Switzerland during the international break. The ex-RB Leipzig star was called up by Slovenia manager Bostjan Cesar earlier this week.

Carrick hoped to have Sesko at his disposal for what was billed as a must-win game, as Matheus Cunha started up front instead. After mustering just four points from their opening four Premier League games, the pressure was on the Red Devils boss.

"I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard, playing at a certain level, achieving certain things on the pitch," Carrick said.

‌



"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, that's just totally not in my thinking, not one part of it. Like, how long I've got. It's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

"I understand what we need to achieve and where we need to be as a football club for the owners, what they expect, for the supporters as much as anything… there's not [much] more important for me than what they expect and what they want to see. I get all that.

"It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results and two or three games too many because I really hate losing. But that doesn't mean that the world caves in. In some minds, it does. It can't for us because we've got to perform, we've got to get wins and we've got a lot of games to plan for. That's exactly what we're doing."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:

Semi-final: Ukraine vs Sweden

Semi-final: Poland vs Albania

Final: Ukraine/Sweden vs Poland/Albania

Play-off Path C:

Semi-final: Turkey vs Romania

Semi-final: Slovakia vs Kosovo

Final: Slovakia/Kosovo vs Turkey/Romania

Play-off Path D:

Semi-final: Denmark vs North Macedonia

Semi-final: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland

Final: Czech Republic/Republic of Ireland vs Denmark/North Macedonia - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr fires brutal dig at fierce rival Conor Benn after Brit's devastating second round defeat by Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr fires brutal dig at fierce rival Conor Benn after Brit's devastating second round defeat by Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas

Chris Eubank Jr brutally mocked his fierce rival Conor Benn after the Brit suffered a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn, 29, was crushed via a second-round stoppage in Las Vegas as they fought for Garcia's WBC welterweight crown.

Benn was dropped by a right hook in round two, and although he managed to beat the count, he struggled to fend off Garcia's subsequent attack, leading to referee Thomas Taylor bringing the fight to a stop, shattering the Brit's world title dream.

It was Benn's first fight at welterweight for four years after he had taken on Eubank Jr at middleweight, meaning he had to cut weight ahead of the fight, something his great rival had to do for their bitter showdowns.

And, Eubank Jr seemed to enjoy his foe's struggles having gone through something similar.

Taking to X shortly after the fight concluded, he posted: 'Welcome to the "fighting after cutting too much weight" club… Enjoy.'

Chris Eubank Jr aimed a brutal dig at Conor Benn after his defeat to Ryan Garcia on Saturday

Benn suffered a heavy defeat by Garcia and his long-time rival Eubank Jr seemed to enjoy it

Eubank Jr had previously posted a photo with Garcia ahead of the fight with the caption: 'Get the job done kid.'

For his two fights against Benn last year, Eubank Jr had to cut down to 160lbs.

He missed that weight for the first bout, before he came under the limit for the second.

Meanwhile, Garcia's triumph over Benn, who was taken to hospital as a precaution, was the Mexican-American's first defence of his WBC crown.

Speaking afterwards, he insisted he hadn't been at full fitness, but outlined his ambitions going forward.

'I have always had the right hand,' he said. 'But I carried a lot of injuries, so I couldn’t really show it.

'I know people question my Mexican heritage because I don’t speak Spanish. But I always feel my people with me and I do it for them. Teofimo Lopez can get it next.

'I want to clean the division out. I want Devin Haney’s a** again, too.'

Sports.title: Why Conor Benn's 85-second humiliation against Ryan Garcia was the inevitable consequence of his fast-tracked career - and how the Brit became a sacrificial pawn in boxing's power struggle, writes JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
The Wizard Of Oz is now a spectacular fantasy production encompassing the inside of the giant globe called The Sphere which looms large over the Las Vegas Strip.

Where the yellow brick road leads for Conor Benn after his one round, one minute and 25 seconds destruction by the fastest gun in Sin City is a question to which nobody had the answer as he was being ferried to hospital for precautionary checks. And may not have for some time to come.

There is no clear pathway back to the heights to which he was thrust all too prematurely and without justification this Saturday night.

Benn had no place being in the same ring as world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia, who is emerging as the golden goose saviour of American and Mexican boxing. Nor had he done anything like enough in his patchwork career thus far to qualify for the honour of topping the bill at an arena as grand as the T-Mobile in as hallowed a home of boxing as Las Vegas.

This was a match made far away from fight heaven, deep in the casino vaults. Benn Jr leaves here millions of dollars the richer but with not so much as a scintilla of evidence that he will ever be able to mix it with the royalty of the ring, in which King Ry sits upon the throne. He has the payoff but not the legacy he craved.

For the second time in as many months English sport comes home from America with its tail between its legs. Only this clinical beat-down of an inferior boxer was aeons more humiliating than the retreat of our footballers from the World Cup. His defeat more comprehensive than that by Argentina.

Conor Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

Benn's humiliating defeat came after he thrust all too prematurely and without justification into the title fight

Benn had no place in being in the same ring as world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia

Little did Benn know, in his delusion of self grandeur, that in return for securing his family’s financial future he was used as a sacrificial pawn in the power struggle for control of big-time boxing between the houses of Queensberry and Matchroom against the arrival of UFC promoter Dana White on their doorstep.

Garcia, younger of the two by a year but a decade wiser, knew. He tried to cushion Benn’s fall from grace by calling him a ‘good dude who I hope can come back from this.’

But as a man who likes to tell it as it is he felt compelled to add: ‘ I knew exactly how the fight would go. Rushing in against me from the start is not a good idea. Not the way to go. You need patience in this game.’

When it was pointed out to him that Benn has not stopped an opponent for more than four years he added: ‘I must be honest. I did not feel any power in his punches.’

Not that there were many of them. Benn’s charge from the first bell was suicidal against the best, fastest and hardest counter puncher in the world. He ran headlong into a hail of Garcia’s trademark left hooks. To note that he lost the first round is as understated as saying that Goliath had a bad day at the office against David. And when in the second Garcia brought into play the right hand which is now almost as deadly as the left Benn was gone in 85 seconds.

Gone crawling on the canvas and still so unsteady when reeled to his feet that the referee let him continue only so far as the next battering.

Garcia observed: ‘It could have been stopped after the first knock down. I looked into his eyes down there and they were glazed over. He was already gone.’

He echoed the pre-fight fears of many of us that Benn could be in critical jeopardy if this went on too long, saying: ‘It would not have been good for Conor if this lasted any further.’

Benn appears to have been a sacrificial pawn in the power struggle for control of big-time boxing between Queensberry and Matchroom against the arrival of UFC promoter Dana White

Has he lived to fight another day? Dana White sounded less than totally convinced: ‘I’ve told Conor to go on holiday with his family and call me when he’s ready to come back. Then we can try to find the right fight for him.’

That would not be at welter after his ‘hellish’ struggle to cut his poundage. But if he can be hammered into oblivion by a 147-pounder what will become of him if he goes back up two divisions to middleweight?

No such doubts hang over Garcia. Having been saluted to the reverberating rafters of the T-Mobile by his half-brother Mexicans in the delirium of their Independence weekend celebrations, this Californian will resume his American love affair in more world title fights against the likes of Devin Haney and Teofimo Lopez.

He, not Conor Benn in his wildest dreams, is the face and the future of boxing over here.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia destroys Conor Benn with brutal second-round TKO to retain WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas showdown
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia destroys Conor Benn with brutal second-round TKO to retain WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas showdown

Ryan Garcia sealed a stunning second-round TKO win over Conor Benn in Las Vegas on Saturday night, retaining his WBC welterweight title in the process.

Benn ran blindly to the slaughter - in a fight which was always a lunge too far - and was left groveling on hands and knees at the feet of the new face of American and Mexican boxing.

Garcia took just four minutes and 25 seconds to devastate and humiliate the upstart son of Nigel the great.

Benn’s predictable sally forth from the first bell was as pointless, desperate and doomed to disaster as The Charge of the Light Brigade.
